title: Maintainability, modularity, packageability, observability, and technical debt
objectives: Define maintainability as change with predictable blast radius, using Well-Architected composable habits.
Separate concerns into business-capability modules rather than one mega-flow or mega-class.
Choose unlocked 2GP packageability for internal apps, with VCS as source of truth, and know org-dependent packages as a transition—not the end state.
Treat observability (Scale Center, Event Monitoring) as how you see debt and runtime behavior, not as a substitute for modular design.
diagnostic_question: A 2,000-element 'monoflow' and unpackaged metadata make every release scary, and nobody can tell which Apex owns quote tax. How do maintainability, modularity, packageability, observability, and technical debt show up in your first 30 days?
definition: Maintainability is the ability to change a Salesforce solution without surprising blast radius. Modularity is separation of concerns into business-capability units. Packageability is delivering those units as second-generation packages (unlocked for internal apps) with version control as source of truth. Observability is seeing runtime and user behavior (Scale Center, Event Monitoring). Technical debt is the gap from that composable end-state—monoflows, duplicated metadata, unmanaged packages. ([Composable](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/composable); [Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers hire architects who can retire a mega-flow, name a package boundary, and say how they will observe the result. 'We will clean it up later' without a module and package plan is how orgs freeze. Observability without modularity just produces better dashboards of a tangle.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a hotel renovated wing by wing. Each wing (module) has its own pipes so you do not shut the whole hotel to fix one shower. Unlocked packages are the work permits and labeled wings you can upgrade independently; git is the blueprint vault, not the front desk org. Sensors on the HVAC (Scale Center, Event Monitoring) are observability. Technical debt is the leaking roof you keep patching with another Flow element instead of isolating the wing.
deeper_explanation: Well-Architected Composable (Adaptable) says composable systems are built from units that can be swapped with stability. Three habits: separation of concerns, interoperability, and packageability. Separate by business capability (jobs to be done), not by reporting structure. Anti-patterns include monoflows that orchestrate everything and massive Apex classes of single-use methods. ([Composable](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/composable))

Packageability means units that can be developed and deployed independently as 2GP—unlocked packages for internal apps, managed 2GP for AppExchange ISVs. First-generation managed packages are out of Well-Architected scope. Source of truth is version control, not the org. Do not duplicate metadata across packages. Start with one meaningful package; too many packages create new bottlenecks. ([Composable](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/composable); [Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm))

Org-dependent unlocked packages defer dependency validation to install time so you can extract metadata that still depends on unpackaged org shape. Well-Architected tools treat them as early-stage or experiment—not the target end-state. Unmanaged packages in production/sandboxes are an anti-pattern. ([Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm); [Packageability tools](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected-tools/guide/adaptable-packageability))

Observability: Scale Center/ApexGuru for throughput and Apex hotspots (ARCH-009); Event Monitoring (often Shield) for user and system activity logs and real-time events. Use them to find debt's runtime cost (slow page, noisy Apex, unused automation), then pay debt by modularizing—not by adding another overlay Flow. Event Monitoring license and event types are edition-sensitive—Needs verification.

mental_model.analogy: Hotel renovated wing by wing: modules are wings, unlocked packages are work permits for a wing, git is the blueprint vault, HVAC sensors are observability, the leaking roof you keep taping is technical debt.
useful_mapping: business capability module → one hotel wing with its own risers
monoflow / mega-class → shutting the whole hotel to fix one shower
unlocked 2GP → wing that can be refurbished and upgraded independently
VCS source of truth → blueprint vault, not the front-desk org copy
org-dependent package → temporary scaffold still tied to the old building
duplicate metadata in two packages → two wings claiming the same room number
Scale Center / Event Monitoring → HVAC and occupancy sensors
technical debt → leaking roof patches that multiply
where_it_breaks: Packages still share an org's governor and data model; wings are not separate hotels (that is multi-org, ARCH-011).
Event Monitoring is not a substitute for debug logs in a developer sandbox.
Unlocked does not mean 'no governance'; CoE still sets standards (ARCH-011).
Sensor data does not remodel the wing by itself.

claims.claim: Composable Salesforce solutions use separation of concerns, interoperability, and packageability. Units should map to business capabilities. Monoflows and massive single-use Apex classes are anti-patterns that hurt maintainability.

Internal business apps should use unlocked second-generation packages; AppExchange distribution uses managed 2GP. Version control is the source of truth, not the org. 1GP managed is not covered as well-architected packageability.

claims.claim: Do not duplicate metadata across packages. Prefer scratch-org package development. Org-dependent unlocked packages are a bridge for unpackaged dependencies, not the ideal end-state. Unmanaged packages in prod/sandboxes are an anti-pattern.
claims.validation: Packageability tools plus DX unlocked guide.

claims.claim: Observability for this lesson includes Scale Center/ApexGuru for runtime performance debt and Event Monitoring for user/system activity telemetry (license-sensitive). Observability finds cost; modular packages reduce blast radius.

claims.claim: Start with a few meaningful packages and iterate. Over-modularizing can slow releases. Refactor packages when business needs or release quality change.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Maintainability is small blast radius. Split by business capability, ship unlocked 2GP from git, observe with Scale Center and Event Monitoring, and retire monoflows as debt—not with another overlay.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I map jobs-to-be-done to modules. I refuse a 2,000-element Flow as architecture. Internal apps get unlocked packages; ISV gets managed 2GP. Org-dependent is a scaffold. I will not duplicate objects across packages. After a slice ships, I look at Scale Center and, if licensed, Event Monitoring to see if the debt actually shrank. I start with one package, not fifty.

terminology.plain: You can change one thing without breaking twelve others.
terminology.precise: Composable units with clear capability mapping, tests, and a known blast radius. Opposite of undocumented monoflows.
terminology.example: Tax logic lives in LAB_TaxService and a small autolaunched Flow, not in Quote, Order, and CPQ overlay Flows.
terminology.non_example: Editing a 2,000-element Flow because 'that is where everything is.'
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Availability: uptime versus ease of change.

terminology.plain: Pieces you can understand and replace.
terminology.precise: Separation of concerns by business capability, plus interoperability contracts (events/APIs) so units are not silos.
terminology.example: Quote-tax capability with a documented invocable method.
terminology.non_example: Folders named after teams (Sales Ops vs IT) with no capability map.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Microservices off-platform: not required for Salesforce modularity.
terminology.boundary: Stateful vs stateless patterns are in Composable state management.

terminology.plain: You can build and ship a unit as a versioned package.
terminology.precise: 2GP unlocked for internal apps; managed 2GP for AppExchange. Git is source of truth. No metadata duplicated across packages.
terminology.example: unlocked package lab-tax 1.3.0 installed in a sandbox.
terminology.non_example: Change-set-only metadata with no package identity.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Unmanaged package: Well-Architected anti-pattern in prod/sandboxes.
terminology.boundary: DEVOPS track owns pipeline mechanics; this lesson owns the architecture choice.

terminology.plain: You can see what the org is doing when it misbehaves.
terminology.precise: Scale Center/ApexGuru for runtime performance; Event Monitoring for activity telemetry. Not the same as a design review (ARCH-012).
terminology.example: ApexGuru still flags the leftover loop in unpackaged automation.
terminology.non_example: A Confluence page with no runtime data.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Debug logs: tactical, not fleet observability.

terminology.plain: Shortcuts that make the next change more expensive.
terminology.precise: Monoflows, mega-classes, unpackaged spaghetti, duplicated metadata, unmanaged packages, org-dependent packages left forever.
terminology.example: Three Flows updating LAB_Quote__c Status__c with no owner.
terminology.non_example: A documented, tested unlocked package that is simply old.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Backlog features: not all backlog is debt.
terminology.boundary: Pay debt in capability slices, not a freeze-the-org rewrite unless NFRs demand it.

terminology.plain: The usual 2GP container for internal Salesforce apps.
terminology.precise: Source-driven, upgradable, metadata editable in the subscriber org (unlike locked managed ISV). Not the AppExchange default.
terminology.non_example: A 1GP managed package from a decade-old packaging org as the well-architected model.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Org-dependent unlocked: same type, weaker dependency validation timing.
terminology.boundary: Profile packing behavior is special-cased in DX docs.

terminology.plain: A package that still leans on unpackaged metadata in the install org.
terminology.precise: Validation at install, not version-create. Cannot depend on other packages the same way. Bridge for tangled orgs.
terminology.example: Extracting LAB_ tax Flow that still references unpackaged fields.
terminology.non_example: The long-term target of 'build once, install anywhere.'

terminology.plain: One giant Flow that tries to run the whole business process.
terminology.precise: Composable anti-pattern: stateful spaghetti, hard to test, huge blast radius. Prefer subflows/invocable Apex per capability.
terminology.example: Quote_Master_Flow with quote, tax, inventory, and email in one canvas.
terminology.non_example: A small record-triggered Flow that calls a subflow.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Flow Orchestrator: a structured alternative, not another 2,000 elements.
terminology.boundary: AUTO track owns Flow mechanics; this lesson owns the architecture smell.

when_to_use: When a change's blast radius is unknown: invest in maintainability and modularity before more features.
When internal metadata should version and upgrade: packageability via unlocked 2GP with git as source of truth.
When you need evidence that debt costs runtime: observability with Scale Center and Event Monitoring, then a slice of refactor.
When a monoflow or mega-class is the bottleneck: treat it as technical debt and extract a capability, not another overlay.
when_not_to_use: Do not create dozens of tiny packages on day one; Composable warns that over-modularizing slows delivery.
Do not use managed 2GP packageability for a typical internal app that should be unlocked.
Do not leave org-dependent unlocked packages as the forever model, or ship unmanaged packages as the architecture.
Do not confuse observability dashboards with a completed modularity program—sensors do not remodel the wing.

interview_questions.question: What does maintainability mean on Salesforce?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You can change a capability with a known blast radius. That comes from modular units, packages, and tests—not from a monoflow nobody owns.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Composable language: capabilities, interoperability, packageability. I contrast a 2,000-element Flow with an invocable tax module. I mention observability as how we see the cost of debt, not as the fix itself.
follow_ups: How do you name a capability?

interview_questions.question: Unlocked versus managed versus unmanaged packages?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Unlocked 2GP for internal apps, git as source of truth. Managed 2GP for AppExchange. Unmanaged in prod is an anti-pattern.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I say 1GP is not the well-architected model. Org-dependent unlocked is a bridge. I do not duplicate objects across packages. Subscriber orgs install versions; they are not the source of truth.
interview_questions.example: Internal lab-quote-tax ships as unlocked package 1.2.0 from source.
tradeoffs: Editability of unlocked versus ISV IP protection
weak_answer_warnings: Change sets are a package type

interview_questions.question: Leadership wants safer weekly tax-rule changes. The tax sits in a giant Quote Flow. Plan?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Extract quote-tax as a module, ship unlocked 2GP, observe hotspots, do not add an overlay Flow.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I inventory metadata, pick a capability name, create lab-quote-tax, replace the tax branch with a subflow/invocable, and time-box org-dependent if fields cannot move. I set an observability baseline. I leave email/inventory for later slices so we do not boil the ocean.
interview_questions.example: Weekly tax upgrade 0.2.0 without touching email Flow.
tradeoffs: Bridge package versus waiting to untangle all fields
follow_ups: How do you test the upgrade?
weak_answer_warnings: Rewrite the whole org this quarter

interview_questions.question: A team proposes 40 unlocked packages next month. Your architecture answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Composable says start with a few meaningful packages. Too many create bottlenecks. Sequence by painful capabilities.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I would approve one or two vertical slices with clear APIs, not a package per object. I would keep a CoE standard for naming and dependencies (ARCH-011). I would watch release cadence; if quality drops, merge or refactor packages.
follow_ups: How do you detect too many packages?
weak_answer_warnings: One package per custom object always

interview_questions.question: Package version create fails because of unpackaged references. Options?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Either move the dependency into the package graph or use org-dependent unlocked as a listed bridge—not unmanaged, not duplicate metadata.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I read the missing type. If it is supported, I add it to the module. If the org is spaghetti, org-dependent with an exit date. I do not copy the object into two packages. I develop in scratch orgs once dependencies are packable.
tradeoffs: Custom metadata in the package versus unpackaged
follow_ups: Can org-dependent depend on other packages?

interview_questions.question: After a 'cleanup' release, CPU is worse. How does observability help?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Compare Scale Center/ApexGuru before and after. You may have added an overlay Flow. Dashboards without a module owner will not fix it.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat observability as evidence. If Event Monitoring is licensed, I check whether users hit a slower page. I look for duplicate automations. I revert or extract, I do not add a fifth Flow. Maintainability work should reduce hotspots, not hide them.
interview_questions.example: ApexGuru still flags SOQL in the leftover overlay.
follow_ups: What if Event Monitoring is not licensed?
How long is a baseline window?
weak_answer_warnings: Observability is only for security teams

interview_questions.question: When is packaging the wrong next step?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When you cannot name a capability, when you would duplicate metadata, or when you would create 40 empty packages. Also when the real issue is a production hotfix with no git.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I stabilize the hotfix process, then package. I do not package secrets. I do not use managed 2GP for a one-off internal script. I do not pretend change sets are 2GP. If Dev Hub is blocked, I still draw modules.
interview_questions.example: Emergency validation rule today; package tax module next sprint.
weak_answer_warnings: Everything must be packaged before any bugfix

interview_questions.question: Teach this topic with a hotel-wing analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Wings are modules, work permits are unlocked packages, blueprint vault is git, HVAC sensors are observability, taped roof is debt. It breaks because wings still share one org's governors and data model.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add org-dependent as scaffolding, unmanaged as an anti-pattern, and 'start with one wing.' Multi-org is a different hotel chain (ARCH-011). Interviewers want 2GP names, not only the metaphor.
interview_questions.example: lab-quote-tax wing versus Quote_Master_Flow hotel shutdown.
